title.narrative: Acre Social and Economic Inclusion and Sustainable Development Project - PROACRE

description.narrative: The Acre Social and Economic Inclusion and Sustainable Development Project for Brazil development objective is to contribute to the Government of Acre's efforts to promote social and economic inclusion of the poorest/most disadvantaged populations living in both urban and isolated/remote rural areas of the state. There are five components to the project. The first component of the project is basic services for isolated communities. This component will support the provision of basic services in health, education and agricultural extension services, including technical and financial assistance, to Acre's dispersed and most isolated communities. The second component of the project is social and economic inclusion in rural areas. This component includes: (i) improving the quality of education and health services in 100 COPs (Pole Communities); and (ii) improving income levels of the population living in these communities by supporting selected production chains. This component will develop activities in COPs, the type of community targeted by the project that has relatively higher level of existing infrastructure and better access to markets. This component will also support professional training for workers of the agricultural and industrial sectors. The third component of the project is entrepreneurship for selected marginal urban communities. The objective of this component is to promote social inclusion of urban communities in areas of high socioeconomic and environmental vulnerability. These urban communities are those located in the bottoms of valleys, close to rivers and in urban marginal areas. In addition, the component will seek to foster entrepreneurship and promote economic empowerment through the promotion of community enterprises, and the expansion of vocational training for professionals and community members. The fourth component of the project is public policy and institutional strengthening. This component aims to: (i) modernize State agencies with emphasis on those involved in Project implementation; (ii) foster decentralization of basic services in health and education, which are part of the responsibilities assigned to municipalities by the Brazilian constitution; and (iii) introduce results-based management strategies in selected sectors. The fifth and final component of the project is project management and information dissemination. This component will support overall project coordination and supervision and will help strengthen the effectiveness and quality of all project operations.

The objective of the Project is to contribute to the Borrower's efforts to promote social and economic inclusion of its rural and urban poor, including its poorest and most disadvantaged population living in isolated areas in the Borrower's territory.

title.narrative: 250 Demonstration Units receiving Project support operational

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved: 93 percent. Initiated under the original project, project activities towards this indicator ceased in 2018 with an achieved results of 210 units. However, the project’s strategy changed and demonstration units in isolated communities were no longer part of the revised strategy. Activities were discontinued to focus on the development of collective action and value chains in communities with higher potential to sustain these activities in the long term.</p>

Number of households with piped sanitation connections

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved: 0 percent. To improve clarity, this indicator was redefined under the Dec-2021 restructuring, replacing the original AF indicator “Increased from zero to 3300 households with piped sanitation connections”. The end target was revised in view of the partial loan cancellation and mobility restrictions induced by the Covid-19 pandemic. Given the significant reduction in especially Marechal and significant sunk cost already incurred by the Project, Acre State will need to provide sanitary connections post-project on its own account. Since the borrower was not able to fully implement the agreed contract to provide septic tanks to 900+ households in Marechal, this contract will also have to be completed post project closure on the borrower’s own account and its successful completion will need to be reported to the Bank.</p>

The end-of-project target of 19,470 represented an increase of 6,170 people over and above the original AF target (13,300).</p>

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved: 79 percent. This indicator was adjusted under the Dec-2021 restructuring. The previous version “Increase from 2200 to 3800 households with piped connections” was introduced under the Sep-2014 AF. In recognition of the different types of water supplied, this indicator was replaced by two separate indicators, i.e., one for urban households "Urban households served with domestic connection for treated water", and another one for indigenous households "Indigenous households served with domestic connection for water for human consumption".</p>

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved: 83 percent. This indicator was introduced under the Dec-2021 restructuring. It replaced the indicator “Reductionof neonatal mortality by place or residence from 11 in 2015 to 9 in 2021” introduced post Sep-2014 AF, aiming at to improve clarity and facilitate measurement. To improve the likelihood of meeting the end-of-project target, the latter was increased from 9 to 10 due to increase in maternal deaths caused by the Covid-19 and sifting prioritization of maternal health care to pregnancies involving Covid-19.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>Target is to achieve a 10% reduction (from 17.29 to 15.45  - definition of this indicator was not changed to reflect the adjusted target) but achievement is a 3.4% increase. This PDO indicator was formally introduced under the Dec-2021 restructuring.It was not part of the AF. However, it was informally introduced in 2016. The indicator is measured as number of deaths per thousand live births. It reached a value of 15.74 in 2019,15.64 in 2020 and 17.89 in 2021. This is mainly due to the COVID-19 pandemic and its negative impacts on poverty, coverage of universal screening programs, access and quality of pediatric care, among others.</p>

title.narrative: Increase in the proportion of live births of mothers with seven or more prenatal consultations from 42.98% in 2015 to 65% in 2021.

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved: 93 percent. This indicator was part of a set of new indicators that replaced the following composite set of Sep-2014 AF indicators: "Increased “successful” and “very successful” deliveries (“Parto bem sucedido” and “muito bem sucedido”) from 0% to 10% in selected maternities from Rio Branco and Jurua"; "Increase the percentage of medical consultations per year per total population of CAPs and COPs from 12% to 72%"; "Proportion of population registered in the family health program (mobile PSF and PACS) from 15% to 90%"; "Reduction of State’s C-Sections in Rio Branco’s maternity from 42% to 28% for low or regular risk pregnancies"; and "Number of health professionals and community agents trained with at least one certified health module in Primary Health Care on both health care lines: maternal/neonatal, and women’s cancer".</p>
<p>During 2020, Covid-19 has had significant adverse impacts on the public health system, including suspension of routine activities in primary care units to prioritize cases of Covid-19 and decreased demand for non-Covid-19 related non-urgent health care services out of fear for Covid-19. This has led to a decrease in the live birthratio compared to previous years. The continuation of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2021 has substantially decreased the likelihood of meeting the original end-of-project target and thus instigated a decrease in the end-of-project target value for this indicator in the Dec 2021 restructuring.</p>
